cases.summary: OpenStack dynamic inventory host gets variables from a group to which it does not belongs.
cases.description:

##### SUMMARY
<!--- Explain the problem briefly -->
During inventory generation by dynamic inventory plugin host gets variables from all groups not only from groups it belongs.

For example I have two openstack instances (FirstServer, SecondServer)

The FirstServer belongs to "linux" group and SecondServer belongs to "windows" group.

group_vars directory have linux.yml and window.yml file for specific variables for groups. 

During ansible-inventory --list (and --export) run I have found that all variables are merged and I have variables from windows group for linux host and visa versa.

The first server have metadata key "groups" with value "stand, linux". The second server have metadata key "groups" with value "stand, windows". So, I have two groups linux and windows.

I have created example project to demonstrate the issue:

https://github.com/ITD27M01/ansible-openstack-bug


The output for "ansible-inventory --list" is: https://github.com/ITD27M01/ansible-openstack-bug/blob/master/openstack-inventory.json#L126

 - Bug Report

Do not include extra details here, e.g. "vyos_command" not "the network module vyos_command" or the full path-->

(or using the ANSIBLE_* environment variables).-->
```

DEFAULT_VAULT_PASSWORD_FILE(env: ANSIBLE_VAULT_PASSWORD_FILE) = /Users/igor.tiunov/tmp/.vault

##### OS / ENVIRONMENT

##### STEPS TO REPRODUCE
<!--- For bugs, show exactly how to reproduce the problem, using a minimal test-case.
For new features, show how the feature would be used. -->

1. Create openstack instances with groups metadata.
2. Create group_vars directory with groups related files and variables,
3. Use openstack inventory plugin for dynamic inventory
4. Read the ansible-inventory --list ouput or ansible-inventory --list --export

  hosts: linux
  gather_facts: no

    - ping:
...
```

<!--- You can also paste gist.github.com links for larger files -->

##### EXPECTED RESULTS
<!--- What did you expect to happen when running the steps above? -->
Hosts have variables only from their groups.

##### ACTUAL RESULTS
<!--- What actually happened? If possible run with extra verbosity (-vvvv) -->
Host gets variables from a group to which it does not belong.

evidence.eventual_fix_title: Do not create group with empty name when region (optional argument) is not given in the openstack connection
evidence.eventual_fix_problem_statement:
Do not create group with empty name when region (optional argument) is not given in the openstack connection

##### SUMMARY
Fixes #42042
Fixes #42040

`region` is an optional connection parameter in Openstack. Currently group with the region name is created automatically, what results in creation of a group with empty name. According to issue #42042 this creates problems. So before creating a group with a region name - check if region is present.

##### ISSUE TYPE
 - Bugfix Pull Request

##### COMPONENT NAME
plugins/inventory/openstack.py
evidence.eventual_fix_diff:
commit 6667ec447466abf1641787afccf9175369319d1f
Author: Artem Goncharov <Artem.goncharov@gmail.com>
Date:   Fri Jul 27 16:02:34 2018 +0200

    fixes #42042 (#42939)
    
    Do not create group with empty name when region (optional argument) is
    not given in the openstack connection

diff --git a/changelogs/fragments/42042-inventory_with_no_region.yaml b/changelogs/fragments/42042-inventory_with_no_region.yaml
new file mode 100644
index 0000000000..65ed6458fd
--- /dev/null
+++ b/changelogs/fragments/42042-inventory_with_no_region.yaml
@@ -0,0 +1,2 @@
+bugfixes:
+- plugins/inventory/openstack.py - Do not create group with empty name if region is not set
diff --git a/lib/ansible/plugins/inventory/openstack.py b/lib/ansible/plugins/inventory/openstack.py
index b2ad6c2ebd..6105a88395 100644
--- a/lib/ansible/plugins/inventory/openstack.py
+++ b/lib/ansible/plugins/inventory/openstack.py
@@ -258,7 +258,8 @@ class InventoryModule(BaseInventoryPlugin, Constructable, Cacheable):
         groups.append(cloud)
 
         # Create a group on region
-        groups.append(region)
+        if region:
+            groups.append(region)
 
         # And one by cloud_region
         groups.append("%s_%s" % (cloud, region))
